title: Get started
text: Immutable documents · Rust · Python · browser Keep the documents. Rebuild the view. CouchDB-inspired map/reduce over an immutable document log. A Rust engine keeps the facts durable; every index and live view is a replaceable cache. Write the computation in AssemblyScript and run the same WebAssembly in Python or a browser worker. Try it in your browser ↗ Build a portable view 01 Append Immutable JSON documents → 02 Map Emit a key and contribution → 03 Fold Derive a rebuildable live view Unreleased development API. This API has not been released on PyPI. These instructions describe the local checkout; remote source and the hosted site can lag changes until publication. Build this checkout or install a wheel built from it. Install from your checkout Build prerequisites are Python 3.11+, Rust/Cargo 1.90+, and a platform C compiler and linker. Run from the repository root: python -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip python -m pip install . python examples/portable_metrics.py On Windows, activate with .venv\Scripts\activate in an MSVC build environment. Node is needed only to author or rebuild views. To build a wheel, run python -m pip wheel . --no-deps --wheel-dir dist , then install the resulting .whl on a matching platform. Installing a built wheel needs neither Rust nor Node. PyPI release setup remains pending. A native metric in a few lines The bundled metrics module maintains count, sum, minimum, maximum, and mean by metric. Start with a fresh metrics.fold log: from foldlitedb import Database, View metrics = View.bundled("metrics") with Database("metrics.fold", metrics) as db: documents = db.add_many([ {"metric": "loss", "value": 4}, {"metric": "loss", "value": 8}, ]) assert list(db.rows())[0].result == { "count": 2, "sum": 12, "min": 4, "max": 8, "mean": 6, } Rust runs both map and reduce in a bounded Wasm interpreter. An accepted batch is appended and synced to the document log. A derived checkpoint lives separately in metrics.fold.cache ; one active database owns the log through metrics.fold.lock . Database and View are the primary names; PortableDatabase and PortableView are aliases. Append freely. Name when useful. Each unnamed add(payload) creates a new observation. Supply a source-scoped ID when identical retries should count once. Documents are immutable; conflicting reuse raises DocumentConflict . with Database("metrics.fold", metrics) as db: saved = db.add({"metric": "loss", "value": 3}, id="measurement-3") assert db.add(saved.payload, id="measurement-3") == saved documents += (saved,) External sources can supply their own IDs and monotonically increasing positions. To represent an update, append another observation and let an ordered view fold its meaning. Read once, follow changes rows() follows bounded snapshot pages. query() also returns a cursor for later changes: with Database("metrics.fold", metrics) as db: snapshot = db.query() db.add({"metric": "loss", "value": 1}) updates = db.changes(since=snapshot.cursor) assert updates.rows[0].result["mean"] == 4 db.checkpoint() Validation, mapping, and reduction finish before a batch is committed. A view error leaves the current batch uncommitted. Checkpoints are optional accelerators, written on request or clean close. A cache can always be reconstructed Keep the document log and exact view module; the cache can be discarded. Reopening verifies the complete log, reuses a valid checkpoint, and executes Wasm only for its uncached suffix. Missing or incompatible checkpoints rebuild from the original batches. Opening with a different module rebuilds its derived view from the same documents. with Database("metrics.fold", metrics) as db: expected = [(r.key, r.state, r.result) for r in db.rows()] db.rebuild() assert [(r.key, r.state, r.result) for r in db.rows()] == expected Rebuild starts a new cursor generation. Its cost is a linear log read plus map/reduce work for uncached batches; no unmeasured throughput is promised. Current indexes and view history grow in host memory. Back up the log: a disposable cache does not make the only source copy disposable. The same module, entirely in a browser Open the static playground , import JSON or JSONL, and watch groups update locally. A dedicated worker executes the same compiled module as Python; JavaScript owns browser grouping and in-memory storage. Export resolved documents before reloading or closing. The browser example includes resource copying and a complete static page. Browser persistence, log/history compaction, and multiple native views per database remain future work. Keep exploring Write a portable view ↗ A complete AssemblyScript module, custom build, and browser integration. The native Python API ↗ Appends, snapshots, changes, checkpoint, and rebuild. Documents and caches ↗ Identity, deterministic folds, durability, and cache validation.

Run it here or in Python. The metrics module accepts documents with a string metric and a finite numeric value . Its map emits the metric as a key. Browser · no backend import { BrowserDatabase } from "./portable/client.js"; const db = await BrowserDatabase.connect(); await db.add({ metric: "latency_ms", value: 42 }); const rows = await db.rows(); console.log(rows[0].result); db.close(); Python · the same metrics.wasm from foldlitedb import Database, View view = View.bundled("metrics") with Database("metrics.fold", view) as db: db.add({"metric": "latency_ms", "value": 42}) row = list(db.rows())[0] print(row.result) Your documents are the source of truth Try the live stream, add a few measurements, then select Rebuild & verify . A fresh in-memory database replays every retained document through the same module and compares its complete view states and results. Existing views keep their cursors. Exported JSON includes document identities, sources, positions, and payloads. Importing it again is an identical replay: each retained document counts once. Changing an existing identity or position fails the whole batch. Use those same records to rebuild the native database. A portable computation preview. This browser database keeps documents and view history in memory. Export them to keep your work. The live stream is simulated locally; this page makes no requests containing your documents. title: Portable views
text:
CouchDB-inspired views, from Python to the browser Write a view once. Run it in either environment. A portable view contains both its map and its reducer. AssemblyScript compiles them into one WebAssembly module, executed by the Rust engine or a browser worker. Try the browser playground Write a custom view Development API. This API has not been released on PyPI. Build this checkout or install a wheel built from it. Each native document log has one derived view; the browser host keeps its documents and view in memory. A native database from Python Build prerequisites are Python 3.11+, Rust/Cargo 1.90+, and a platform C compiler and linker. From the repository root: python -m pip install . python examples/portable_metrics.py The Rust engine and precompiled view modules are included. Node is needed only for authoring or rebuilding AssemblyScript. To produce a wheel locally, run python -m pip wheel . --no-deps --wheel-dir dist . Installing the resulting wheel on a matching platform needs no compiler. See environment setup for virtual-environment and Windows notes. Start the following example with fresh database files: from foldlitedb import Database, View view = View.bundled("metrics") with Database("metrics.fold", view) as db: documents = db.add_many([ {"metric": "loss", "value": 4}, {"metric": "loss", "value": 8}, ]) assert list(db.rows())[0].result["mean"] == 6 snapshot = db.query() db.add({"metric": "loss", "value": 3}) assert db.changes(since=snapshot.cursor).rows[0].result["mean"] == 5 retained = tuple(db.documents()) Rust owns the append-only document log, immutable identity, derived checkpoints, group states, snapshots, and changes. Its bounded Wasm interpreter executes both mapping and reduction. The log is independent of the module; a checkpoint is a disposable cache. rows() follows paginated snapshots; explicit query() and changes() support resumable reads. The Python reference covers every portable method. Two bundled views Metrics accepts payloads with a string metric and finite numeric value . Valid documents emit one number under their metric key; malformed shapes, missing fields, nulls, and nonnumeric values emit nothing. States contain {count,sum,min,max} ; finalized results add mean . Empty states use null minimum, maximum, and mean. This view supports merge. Invalid contributions, states, and numeric overflow fail. Catalogue accepts {category:string,id:string,title:string,deleted?:boolean} . Each category folds item IDs to their latest titles. An event with {category,id,deleted:true} removes that item. Finalization returns {count,items:{id:title}} . Event order matters, so this view does not support merge. Malformed documents emit nothing; item IDs are limited to 65,535 UTF-16 code units. Author a complete view Use Node.js 20+ and the pinned SDK dependencies. The bundled build handles exactly metrics and catalogue ; it does not discover additional files: npm ci --prefix views npm run build --prefix views npm test --prefix views npm run check --prefix views For a custom module, save this complete source as views/assembly/examples/metric-totals.ts . It groups numeric values by metric and returns a running total. The SDK handles UTF-8 buffers, finite JSON, allocation, dispatch, and error envelopes. import { JSON, View, Emission, object, numeric, number, dispatch } from "../sdk"; export { abi_version, input_ptr, input_capacity, output_ptr } from "../sdk"; class MetricTotals extends View { constructor() { super("metric-totals", false, "1", "1"); } map(document: JSON.Value): Emission[] { const doc = object(document); if (doc == null) return []; const metric = doc.get("metric"); const value = doc.get("value"); if (metric == null || metric.type != JSON.Types.String || !numeric(value)) { return []; } return [new Emission(metric, value!)]; } identity(): JSON.Value { return JSON.Value.from(0); } add(state: JSON.Value, values: JSON.Arr): JSON.Value { if (!numeric(state)) return this.fail("Invalid total state"); let total = number(state); for (let i = 0; i < values.length; i++) { const value = values.at(i); if (!numeric(value)) return this.fail("Expected a numeric contribution"); total += number(value); } if (!isFinite(total)) return this.fail("Total overflowed"); return JSON.Value.from(total); } finalize(state: JSON.Value): JSON.Value { if (!numeric(state)) return this.fail("Invalid total state"); return state; } } const view = new MetricTotals(); export function execute(length: i32): i32 { return dispatch(view, length); } Compile from views/ using the same compiler settings as the bundled modules. These are POSIX-shell commands: cd views mkdir -p .build JSON_MODE=naive node node_modules/assemblyscript/bin/asc.js \ assembly/examples/metric-totals.ts \ --outFile .build/metric-totals.wasm \ --transform json-as --runtime incremental \ --maximumMemory 256 --initialMemory 16 --stackSize 32768 \ --use abort=assembly/sdk/index/abort \ --optimizeLevel 3 --shrinkLevel 1 While still in views/ , generate the digest manifest used by the browser. The descriptor is read from the compiled module, so it matches the view name, version, state version, and merge capability: node --input-type=module <<'JS' import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'; import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'; const bytes = await readFile('.build/metric-totals.wasm'); const module = new WebAssembly.Module(bytes); if (WebAssembly.Module.imports(module).length) throw new Error('Unexpected imports'); const { exports: api } = new WebAssembly.Instance(module); const input = new TextEncoder().encode('{"op":"descriptor"}'); new Uint8Array(api.memory.buffer).set(input, api.input_ptr()); const length = api.execute(input.length); const response = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode( new Uint8Array(api.memory.buffer, api.output_ptr(), length))); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(response.error); const manifest = { abi: 1, module: 'metric-totals.wasm', sha256: createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex'), descriptor: response.ok, }; await writeFile('.build/metric-totals.json', JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2) + '\n'); JS cd .. Back at the repository root, load the same bytes from Python. This example follows the custom compilation steps above: import json from pathlib import Path from foldlitedb import Database, View manifest = json.loads(Path("views/.build/metric-totals.json").read_text()) custom = View("views/.build/metric-totals.wasm", sha256=manifest["sha256"]) with Database(":memory:", custom) as db: db.add_many([{"metric": "loss", "value": 4}, {"metric": "loss", "value": 8}]) assert list(db.rows())[0].result == 12 The map receives payloads only, not host IDs or positions. Include domain metadata inside the payload if your computation needs it. Keys, states, and contributions can be structured JSON. State is passed explicitly to every update; requests must not depend on mutable module globals, clocks, randomness, or undeclared external data. Hosts instantiate the module afresh for operations. add must preserve contribution order and produce equivalent state when an input sequence is split into successive batches. Implement merge and set mergeable=true only when compatible independent states can be combined correctly. The example leaves merge disabled. Bump the view version for changed behavior and the state version for incompatible formats; rebuild the module and manifest together. A new compiler can also change the module digest. Use the module on a static website The playground imports JSON arrays or JSONL, appends measurements, streams simulated updates, exports resolved records, and verifies replay. All document processing stays in its worker. The same module bytes power the Python example; JavaScript owns browser grouping and storage. The Rust document-log engine is not part of the browser build. To create your own page, copy the installed package's browser files and bundled modules. Run this Python from the repository root: from pathlib import Path from foldlitedb import portable_assets target = Path("browser-demo/portable") target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) for resource in portable_assets().iterdir(): if resource.is_file(): (target / resource.name).write_bytes(resource.read_bytes()) Save this as browser-demo/index.html . Browser methods are asynchronous; addMany returns a batch-result object, while Python's add_many returns a tuple of documents. Foldlite DB in the browser 
Loading…
python -m http.server 8000 --directory browser-demo Open http://localhost:8000 ; opening the file directly is insufficient for module workers and fetch. Production deployments can serve these files over HTTPS. Keep client.js , worker.js , and host.js together. For the custom totals view, copy views/.build/metric-totals.wasm and metric-totals.json into browser-demo/portable/ , then change the connection to: const db = await BrowserDatabase.connect({ name: 'metric-totals', base: new URL('./portable/', import.meta.url), }); The browser verifies the manifest's SHA-256 and descriptor before execution. db.info contains initial stats; await db.stats() exposes the current module digest, descriptor, checkpoints, document count, cursor, and Wasm memory size. Compare module_sha256 with Python's View.sha256 to confirm the exact artifact. query({limit,cursor,after,key}) returns snapshot pages; continue with both returned cursor and after. rows({limit,key}) collects all pages into an array. changes(cursor,{limit}) returns one change page; continue with its returned cursor until complete. ingest(resolvedDocuments) replays exported records with their retained identities and positions. add(payload,{id,source,position}) accepts an optional explicit identity. export() returns all resolved records. replay() rebuilds with original committed batches and reports equivalence of keys, states, and results. The computation contract and limits Operation Input Output descriptor Module request Name, view version, state version, ABI, merge capability map A batch of document payloads An emission array per document, including zero emissions identity Empty request Initial JSON state for a group add State and ordered contributions Updated JSON state finalize State Public JSON result merge Two compatible states Combined state, when supported The v1 ABI uses UTF-8 JSON with a 256 KiB request limit and a separate 256 KiB response limit, both including envelopes. Modules have no host imports and at most 16 MiB of linear memory. The native host imposes a fuel budget. The browser client runs a dedicated worker with a 15-second default deadline, configurable through timeoutMs from 1 through 60,000 milliseconds. Expiry terminates the worker and loses its in-memory state. Both hosts limit an ingestion batch to 1024 documents and 4096 emissions, and snapshot pages to 1024 entries. Encoded map and per-group add requests can reach the ABI byte limit earlier. The browser additionally caps retained documents at 20,000 and 16 MiB of encoded records, distinct groups at 4096, and history at 100,000 entries and 32 MiB of encoded rows. Its public request envelope is capped at 4 MiB. These are component limits, not a bound on the whole browser process. A failing batch does not commit a prefix. Portable JSON numbers use IEEE-754 double precision, as in JavaScript. Python rejects integer inputs that cannot be represented exactly as doubles; use strings for exact large identifiers. Positions and cursor sequences are nonnegative JavaScript-safe integers. Floating-point sums preserve ordered inputs; arbitrary merge trees can change rounding. See numerical reproducibility . Retain documents; regenerate views Keep the document log and exact compiled module. A persistent metrics.fold log has separate metrics.fold.cache and metrics.fold.lock siblings. One active owner holds the log. Accepted immutable batches are synced before acknowledgement; clean close or checkpoint() writes an atomic derived snapshot. Reopen verifies the complete log, reuses a matching cache prefix, and executes Wasm for only the uncached suffix. Missing, corrupt, or different-module caches rebuild from the original batches. To change computation, open the same log with the new module; documents remain unchanged. A human version label cannot override a changed digest. Keep the previous module if its previous result must remain reproducible. rebuild() explicitly recomputes the current view, checkpoints it, and starts a new cursor generation. Reconstruction is a linear log read plus map/reduce work for uncached batches; current indexes and history grow in host memory. Cache acceleration avoids computation, rather than the full validation read, and has no unmeasured throughput guarantee. with Database("metrics.fold", view) as live: expected = [(row.key, row.state, row.result) for row in live.rows()] live.rebuild() assert [(row.key, row.state, row.result) for row in live.rows()] == expected To copy resolved documents into a separate log, preserve their original order: with Database("copy.fold", view) as rebuilt: rebuilt.ingest(retained) assert list(rebuilt.rows())[0].result["mean"] == 5 For larger streams, iterate db.ingest_many(records, batch_size=100) ; each yielded result commits one bounded batch. db.documents(limit=100) exports resolved records at a pinned snapshot. Browser exports include an additional engine sequence field; Python accepts them after constructing Document objects: import json from pathlib import Path from foldlitedb import Document, Database, View view = View.bundled("metrics") records = json.loads(Path("exported-documents.json").read_text(), parse_int=float) documents = [Document(r["id"], r["payload"], int(r["position"]), r["source"]) for r in records] with Database("from-browser.fold", view) as db: for result in db.ingest_many(documents): print(result.inserted, result.replayed) The final snippet expects an exported JSON array from the metrics view. Browser payload numbers use IEEE-754 doubles; parse_int=float preserves those semantics even when a large double is serialized without a decimal point. Safe source positions are converted back to Python integers when constructing documents. Preserve input order; preserve batch boundaries too if exact engine sequence values matter. Compare computation outputs rather than database-local cursors. A new database or rebuilt cache receives a new generation, so obtain new cursors even when results match. A valid checkpoint preserves cursors across an ordinary reopen. Native documents persist in the log; a cache can always be reconstructed. Back up the log or an authoritative external stream: deleting the only source copy loses data. Browser state is in memory and is discarded on reload or close() . Export before closing and ingest those records into a new worker to restore it. Persistent browser storage, log/history compaction, and multiple native views per database remain future extensions. See the document and cache model .

title: Python API
text: Reference · development API The Python API Database is the Rust-native engine for immutable document logs and rebuildable Wasm views. View identifies the complete compiled computation. There is one storage and computation path. View and packaged assets View(module, *, sha256=None) View.bundled(name="metrics") → View portable_assets() → importlib.resources Traversable Import these names from foldlitedb . module accepts Wasm bytes or a filesystem path. A View stores immutable module bytes and their sha256 ; an optional digest must match. Modules range from 1 byte through 16 MiB. The native database validates exports, imports, ABI, and descriptor when opening. bundled accepts "metrics" or "catalogue" and verifies the manifest digest. Metrics returns {count,sum,min,max,mean} ; catalogue returns {count,items} . See accepted payloads . portable_assets() exposes modules, manifests, and browser hosts; copy files with each resource's read_bytes() method. PortableView is an exact alias of View . It does not select another engine. Database Database(path, view=None) A Rust-native database executing one complete Wasm view. view accepts a View , Wasm bytes, or a module path; omit it for bundled metrics. path accepts a filesystem path or ":memory:" . Parent directories must already exist. A persistent path is an append-only document log, with .cache and .lock siblings. Exactly one active owner may open it. Use a context manager or close() . Clean close checkpoints persistent derived state and releases ownership. Closing is idempotent; later operations raise DatabaseError . PortableDatabase is an exact alias. Reopen validates the complete log and reuses a compatible cache, then replays any uncached suffix. A missing or invalid cache rebuilds. Different module bytes automatically rebuild the view from the same documents. Reconstruction creates a new cursor generation; a valid checkpoint preserves generation across reopen. Old external-database files are not this log format. from foldlitedb import Database, View with Database(":memory:", View.bundled("metrics")) as db: original = db.add({"metric": "loss", "value": 4}, id="a") assert db.add(original.payload, id="a") == original snapshot = db.query() db.add({"metric": "loss", "value": 8}) assert db.changes(since=snapshot.cursor).rows[0].result["mean"] == 6 retained = tuple(db.documents()) assert db.stats()["documents"] == 2 with Database(":memory:") as replay: assert replay.ingest(retained).inserted == 2 assert replay.ingest(retained).replayed == 2 Append and replay db.add(payload, *, id=None, source="default", position=None) → Document db.add_many(payloads, *, source="default") → tuple[Document, ...] db.ingest(documents) → IngestResult db.ingest_many(documents, *, batch_size=100) → iterator[IngestResult] add appends one finite JSON payload and returns its resolved Document(id, payload, position, source) . Omitted IDs are generated; omitted positions start at zero and advance per source. An identical named add or replay at an existing source position reuses the original document. Conflicting reuse fails; previously unseen positions must advance that source. IDs and sources are nonempty strings of at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; positions range from zero through 2**53 - 1 . add_many eagerly consumes one iterable of payloads and commits atomically. Its returned records preserve input order. Every member is one payload, including an entire array; empty input returns () . Retrying unnamed payloads appends new observations. Documents are immutable; append a new observation to express a change. ingest takes explicit Document instances with retained identities, positions, and payloads. Its result contains inserted , replayed , and sequence . Identical replay performs no map work. ingest_many is lazy: each yielded result commits a separate batch of 1–1024 records, defaulting to 100. A later error preserves earlier committed batches. An atomic batch has at most 1024 documents and 4096 emissions. The complete map request, including its envelope and newly inserted payloads, must fit 256 KiB; per-group add requests, states, and results must fit their own buffers. The log frame limit is 8 MiB. Reduce batch size for larger payloads. Validation, map, reducer, and limit errors leave the current batch uncommitted; successful persistent batches are synced before acknowledgement. Finite JSON uses IEEE-754 doubles and at most 64 nesting levels. Python rejects integer inputs not exactly representable as doubles. Nonfinite values and invalid Unicode scalar strings fail. Use strings for arbitrary-precision identifiers. Rows, snapshots, and changes db.rows(*, key=<omitted>, limit=100) → iterator[Row] db.query(*, key=<omitted>, limit=100, cursor=None, after=None) → Snapshot db.changes(*, since, limit=100) → ChangePage rows lazily follows snapshot pages, pinning the committed prefix on first iteration. limit is a page size from 1 through 1024, not a total row limit. Omit key for every group or supply any JSON key, including null, for exact filtering. Rows follow canonical JSON lexical order consistent with the browser. No operation lock spans a yield into application code. A Row has key , reducer state , finalized result , and committed sequence . A Snapshot has rows , cursor , after , and complete . Continue with both returned cursor and after token, preserving the key filter. New ingestion does not change the pinned snapshot. with Database(":memory:") as db: db.add_many([ {"metric": "a", "value": 2}, {"metric": "b", "value": 8}, ]) page = db.query(limit=1) snapshot_cursor = page.cursor rows = list(page.rows) while not page.complete: page = db.query(limit=1, cursor=page.cursor, after=page.after) rows.extend(page.rows) assert [row.key for row in rows] == ["a", "b"] db.add({"metric": "a", "value": 4}) changes = db.changes(since=snapshot_cursor, limit=1) assert changes.rows[0].result["mean"] == 3 while not changes.complete: changes = db.changes(since=changes.cursor, limit=1) changes returns committed group postimages after a snapshot or change cursor. since=0 reads retained history from the start. A page has rows , continuation cursor , and complete ; continue with that cursor. Repeated changes to a key in one batch coalesce. A page can split group updates from one batch. Zero-emission documents still advance progress. Cursors bind to the database generation and exact module. Checkpointed reopen can reuse them; rebuild, cache reconstruction, or module replacement expires them. A new database or browser worker cannot reuse another's cursor. There is no history compaction API. Checkpoint, rebuild, export, and inspect db.checkpoint() → dict db.rebuild() → dict db.documents(*, limit=100) → iterator[Document] db.stats() → dict db.close() checkpoint atomically persists the current derived snapshot and returns stats plus checkpointed: true . Clean close also checkpoints. The cache is optional and is not rewritten after every append. Encoded snapshots are capped at 1 GiB. Checkpoint failures are reported, including during close; the synced source log remains intact and close releases ownership even on failure. rebuild replays original log batches through the current module, starts a new cursor generation, writes a checkpoint, and returns stats plus rebuilt: true . Documents remain unchanged. with Database("maintenance.fold") as db: db.add_many([{"metric": "loss", "value": 4}, {"metric": "loss", "value": 8}]) expected = [(row.key, row.state, row.result) for row in db.rows()] assert db.checkpoint()["checkpointed"] is True assert db.rebuild()["rebuilt"] is True assert [(row.key, row.state, row.result) for row in db.rows()] == expected documents exports resolved records in original ingestion order at a snapshot pinned on first iteration. Page size is 1–1024. Back up these records or the log and retain exact view artifacts; the cache can be regenerated. Re-import through ingest or ingest_many . stats includes documents , groups , sequence , cursor , generation , module_sha256 , descriptor , and source checkpoints . storage is "append-only-log" or "memory" . The cache object reports status , bytes , and log_offset ; replay reports processed batches and documents ; log reports bytes , batches , and recovered_tail_bytes . Engine sequence counts inserted documents and changed group states, rather than documents alone. Cache status describes checkpoint handling; replay counts make uncached reconstruction visible. Reopening always verifies the complete log, even with a valid cache. Current retained documents, indexes, and view history grow in host memory; there is no compaction or bounded total-memory guarantee. Errors and recovery DatabaseError extends ValueError . Validation and Wasm failures raise it; conflicting replay, source ordering, and invalid cursors use DocumentConflict , SourceOrderError , and CursorExpired where identified. A missing compiled extension raises an actionable RuntimeError . Opening an already-owned log fails. Complete log corruption fails rather than skipping records; only an incomplete final frame is recoverable as an interrupted append. A cache failure can be repaired by reconstruction. If an I/O error makes an append's acknowledgement uncertain, close, reopen, and retry using explicit resolved identities. Keep backups of source data.

title: Documents and caches
text: The model Documents and rebuildable caches Documents are immutable facts. A view is a deterministic fold over those facts. Persist the facts, verify cache dependencies, and make reconstruction an ordinary operation. Names are optional; documents are immutable add(payload) assigns an internal ID. Equal unnamed payloads are separate observations. A caller-supplied ID tells the host that an identical repeated call refers to one observation. An identical named retry skips mapping and keeps its original position, even after the source advances. Reusing that identity with different content is a conflict. Represent a lifecycle change by appending another document, then fold its meaning in an ordered view. The log never updates an accepted document in place. Positions track a source A position identifies a document's offset in its source. Automatic positions start at zero and follow that source's committed checkpoint. External logs can supply increasing offsets with gaps. from foldlitedb import Database, SourceOrderError with Database(":memory:") as db: first = db.add({"metric": "loss", "value": 4}, source="training.log", position=10) db.add({"metric": "loss", "value": 8}, source="training.log", position=40) assert db.add(first.payload, source="training.log", position=10) == first assert db.stats()["checkpoints"]["training.log"] == 40 try: db.add({"metric": "loss", "value": 3}, source="training.log", position=30) except SourceOrderError: pass else: raise AssertionError("New records cannot arrive behind the checkpoint") IDs and positions are scoped to a source. An existing position can identify a replay without a supplied ID; payload and any supplied ID must match. Previously unseen positions behind committed progress fail. Positions range from zero through 2**53 - 1 . Avoid mixing generated positions with external offsets unless they share a progression. Order belongs to the input Per-key reduction follows ingestion order, including document and emission order inside a batch. Source offsets do not sort documents across sources; timestamps do not reorder an existing fold. Applications choose domain order before ingestion and preserve it during replay. Maps receive payloads; the host owns identities, source positions, deduplication, and batches. Include needed domain metadata inside a payload. The bundled catalogue demonstrates a structured lifecycle fold whose answer can change if events are reordered. Views must give equivalent state when the same ordered contribution sequence is split across successive add calls. Batch boundaries cannot define application semantics. Engine sequence values do depend on batches because they include document and changed-group records. The native log retains original accepted batches for exact internal reconstruction. The document log is durable A persistent Database("live.fold") owns three paths: the document log live.fold , a disposable checkpoint live.fold.cache , and an ownership lock live.fold.lock . One active owner may open the log. Close it before another process or instance opens it. ":memory:" creates no persistent files. An accepted batch is stored in a checksummed, hash-linked log frame and synced before acknowledgement. Validation, map, and reducer failures commit none of the current batch. ingest_many commits separate batches as iteration proceeds; earlier successful batches survive a later error. If an I/O failure interrupts acknowledgement, reopen and retry explicit identities to resolve whether a batch committed. Reopening validates the complete log. A partial final frame can be truncated as an interrupted write; complete corrupt frames fail explicitly. Recovery does not skip invalid committed documents. Preserve a backup of the log or an external authoritative document stream. Deleting the only source copy loses data. A checkpoint is a hint Document indexes, source checkpoints, reduced states, results, and history can all be derived again. checkpoint() atomically writes their current snapshot, and clean close also checkpoints. Encoded snapshots are capped at 1 GiB; checkpoint errors are reported even on close, while accepted log data remains intact. A failed close releases its native handle. The engine checks cache format, log identity, exact module digest, and the verified log-prefix offset and digest before reuse. With a valid snapshot, reopen loads its prefix and executes Wasm only for uncached suffix batches. Missing, corrupt, or incompatible cache data causes reconstruction from the document log. The log still must be read and verified linearly on every reopen; a checkpoint avoids computation, not that validation read. Checksums detect corruption, rather than authenticate files against someone who can rewrite them. from foldlitedb import View view = View.bundled("metrics") with Database("live.fold", view) as live: live.add_many([ {"metric": "loss", "value": 4}, {"metric": "loss", "value": 8}, ]) expected = [(r.key, r.state, r.result) for r in live.rows()] retained = tuple(live.documents()) live.checkpoint() live.rebuild() assert [(r.key, r.state, r.result) for r in live.rows()] == expected with Database("copy.fold", view) as copied: copied.ingest(retained) assert [(r.key, r.state, r.result) for r in copied.rows()] == expected assert copied.ingest(retained).replayed == 2 rebuild() replays the existing log and writes a fresh checkpoint without changing its documents. It starts a new cursor generation. Export and re-import also preserve results when order is retained, but may use different batches and therefore different engine sequences. Preserve resolved records rather than payloads alone if identities and source progress must survive. Rebuild performs linear log I/O plus map/reduce work for uncached batches and emissions. Current indexes and history grow in host memory with the data; limits on one call are not a bound on total data. There are no measured rebuild-throughput guarantees or compaction API yet. A view revision is exact module bytes The module SHA-256 identifies mapping, reduction, state format, compiler, and SDK runtime. A matching human version label cannot override different bytes. Bump the view version for changed behavior and the state version for incompatible state schemas, then rebuild the module and manifest. The document log is independent of the module. Open it with another module to automatically rebuild its derived view in place. Retain the previous bytes to reproduce the previous computation. A new module that cannot process the retained documents raises an error; it does not discard them. Rebuilding starts a new cursor generation even if the outputs happen to match. Deterministic views use explicit inputs and state rather than clocks, randomness, mutable globals, or undeclared external data. Hosts instantiate Wasm modules afresh for operations. Reference inputs must remain reproducible, not merely have a remembered version label. A fold is not automatically mergeable; implement merge only when its laws hold. Stable reads and generation boundaries A snapshot cursor names a database generation, exact module, and committed prefix. Continue a query with both its cursor and after token; new documents do not change that snapshot. Changes carry resulting key states after the chosen cursor, coalesced per key within a batch. A page can split a batch's group updates; zero-emission documents still advance progress. A valid native checkpoint preserves generation and cursors across reopen. Explicit rebuild, a missing or invalid checkpoint requiring reconstruction, or a changed module starts a new generation and expires old cursors. A fresh browser worker also has a new identity. Obtain a new snapshot after reconstruction rather than transferring cursors. Row and document iterators release the engine between pages. No operation lock spans a yield into application code, although a persistent database retains its file-ownership lock until close. History is currently retained; there is no history compaction or reader-expiry policy. The same computation; browser memory The browser worker loads identical Wasm bytes, while JavaScript owns grouping, documents, and history. It does not run the Rust log engine. There is no IndexedDB persistence yet. Reload, close, or a worker deadline discards memory; export resolved records and ingest them into a new worker to restore the view. The browser preview rejects batches above its document, group, history, and byte limits; see component limits . Browser replay() constructs a separate worker-side replay with the original batches and compares keys, states, and results, leaving the current worker's cursors intact. Numerical reproducibility Payloads, keys, states, and results use finite IEEE-754 doubles, matching JavaScript numbers. Python rejects integer inputs that cannot be represented exactly as a double. Encode arbitrary-precision identifiers as strings. Positions and engine sequences remain nonnegative JavaScript-safe integers. JSON nesting is bounded to 64 levels. The same module and canonical key rules give both hosts the same supported computation. Neither adds Python arbitrary-precision arithmetic. Floating-point addition is not associative: arbitrary merge trees can change rounding. Preserve input order and partition/merge plans when exact agreement matters. Merge compatible states with disjoint coverage, rather than finalized means.
